subject: merge of multirec-io into dev, closing in on rmr 1.3

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: merge of multirec-io into dev, closing in on rmr 1.3
parts:
Hi this morning I merged multirec-io into dev, which means we are getting a step closer to 1.3.  This was done after multirec-io passed all tests, so I think dev is in a state where people who are particularly eager to reap the speed benefits should start kicking the tires. Please don't email me with "I run my program and it takes the same time as with 1.2.2" that was not the point. The point was to better support a vectorized style or programming that is the main approach to efficient R development. If you don't use the new vectorized features, you are not going to see much of a difference. The idea is that processing one record at a time in the map function is inefficient with small records. It's inefficient to parse or unserialize one small record at a time, it's harder to make use of vectorized functions in the map and so forth. Now you can process multiple records at once. You can also output multiple records in a single keyval call, using the vectorized option. There isn't much documentation for the new features yet but you can read the comments to issues #66 and can take a look at vectorized-API.R under tests in the source. There are also preliminary speed tests in the comments of that file. I also slipped in some improvements in the support of  structured data, whereby you can ask to see your data as a data.frame and not a list at different points in the API, maybe I should have held those back for a later time, but at least I wanted to take them into account as the API was being reorganized, to be more consistent. More work is needed on defining exactly what the structured conversion does and on the implementation side.


Antonio

messages.subject: Re: merge of multirec-io into dev, closing in on rmr 1.3
parts:
Just to let people know that at this point dev passes all the tests on AWS/CDH3 (an extended set that includes the work tracked in #90 and #91) so I created a release branch rmr-1.3 which is under feature freeze and a release candidate. People are encouraged to test it at this time and in particular there one outstanding issue to test this on Apache Hadoop 1.0.2, so if anyone is running that and cold do an R CMD check rmr/pkg or whatever is your installation directory and report back that would be great. It can take  hours, just so you are prepared. Thanks


Antonio
